title: Vote on clarifying the day partition transform result type as date in the spec
summary: Andrei Tserakhau called a vote on the spec clarification in PR #16446. It changes the `day` partition transform's result type in the transform table from `int` to `date`, matching what Java, PyIceberg, Rust and C++ already write in manifests (the Avro `date` logical type), and adds a note that readers must also accept plain `int` values, read as days since 1970-01-01. He described it as a clarification with no behavioral change: the physical 4-byte day count is unchanged and no existing manifests are affected. The ambiguity had come up repeatedly, most recently as an interop failure in iceberg-go. A vote was held because changes under `format/` require one. All eight votes on the first day were +1. Russell Spitzer added that a vote was not really needed and that the PR mainly needs more committer approvals. No result message appears in the thread.

positions.stance: The spec should state `date` as the result type of the `day` transform and require readers to also accept plain `int`, documenting what implementations already do.
Votes +1 (binding) and considers a vote unnecessary since this is existing behavior; the PR needs more committer approvals.

outcome.note: No result is announced in the thread. Votes cast were all +1: five binding and three non-binding, including the proposer's.

why_it_matters: Implementations get an unambiguous rule for the day transform: write `date`, and accept `int` when reading.
